_help: Table read by install.py. Each platform says where the skills, agents and commands go, in which format and which documentation backs the path. {HOME} is the user's folder (or --target); {LOCALAPPDATA} is %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows (or <target>/AppData/Local). 'variable' is the environment variable that, if it exists and --target was not given, wins over 'default'. Checked against the documentation on 15-10-2026.
exclude_rationale: Only generated files are excluded (bytecode, run outputs). tests/ IS installed: every SKILL.md says to run scripts/<script>.py --test, which reads tests/, and the auditor uses it to confirm the method works where it was installed.
profile_template_rationale: The scripts look for the template in <root>/profiles/_template.yaml, with <root> = three folders above scripts/ (skills/<method>/scripts/x.py). In a copy, <root> is the platform's configuration folder, so the template is copied there. With --link it is not needed: the script resolves the link and reaches the repo.
extras_rationale: orchestrate, research and map-context cite ARCHITECTURE.md («repo root»). A copy has no repo root: a copy of it is left next to orchestrate's SKILL.md.

claude-code.name: Claude Code (without the plugin)
claude-code.orchestration: with agents (the main conversation launches cartographer, researcher, executor and auditor)
claude-code.note: The recommended route is the plugin (/plugin marketplace add ingeniero-agentico/ingeniero-agentico). This copy is the alternative without GitHub; do not install both at once.

claude-desktop.name: Claude Desktop and claude.ai (chat and Cowork)
claude-desktop.plugin_zip_rationale: mcp/ goes because plugin.json declares the MCP server with ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/mcp/server.py: the chat ignores it (it is local), Cowork starts it if the session runs on your computer.
claude-desktop.orchestration: chat: no agents (stages in sequence); Cowork: loads agents/
claude-desktop.note: One ZIP per skill with the <skill>/ folder as its only top level (Customize > Skills), and one ZIP with the whole plugin (Customize > Plugins > Add > Upload plugin). Needs code execution turned on.

codex.name: Codex (OpenAI): CLI, IDE and app
codex.commands_rationale: Codex invokes skills with $name or /skills; /new-task only wraps orchestrate, so $orchestrate is used.
codex.orchestration: with TOML subagents (converted from agents/); if it does not launch them, in sequence
codex.note: Codex reads skills from $HOME/.agents/skills (user) and .agents/skills (repo). Agents are converted to TOML with name, description and developer_instructions.

cursor.name: Cursor
cursor.commands_rationale: Cursor is migrating commands to skills (/migrate-to-skills); orchestrate is invoked by typing /orchestrate.
cursor.orchestration: with subagents (~/.cursor/agents); if it does not launch them, in sequence
cursor.note: Cursor also reads ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills: if you already installed for Claude Code or Codex, there is no need to repeat.

gemini.name: Gemini CLI
gemini.commands_rationale: Gemini commands are TOML with another syntax; orchestrate activates itself from its description (activate_skill).
gemini.orchestration: with subagents (~/.gemini/agents); a subagent does not launch another, same as in Claude Code
gemini.note: Gemini also reads ~/.agents/skills (alias with precedence). Agents keep only name and description: Claude's tools and model are not valid in Gemini.

hermes.name: Hermes Agent (Nous Research)
hermes.agents_rationale: Hermes does not load agent definitions from files: it delegates with the delegate_task tool (generic children with goal and context).
hermes.commands_rationale: Every Hermes skill is already a /<skill-name> command; /orchestrate replaces /new-task.
hermes.orchestration: with delegate_task (generic children) or in sequence
sources: installed code v0.21.4: hermes_constants.py (get_skills_dir = HERMES_HOME/skills; on Windows HERMES_HOME = %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes) and agent/skill_utils.py (recursive SKILL.md search, skills.external_dirs)
hermes.note: Alternative without copying: add the repo's skills/ folder to skills.external_dirs in config.yaml (you do it; install.py does not touch config.yaml).

agents.name: Any agent compatible with Agent Skills (shared folder ~/.agents/skills)
agents.agents_rationale: The Agent Skills standard does not define agents or commands.
agents.note: Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI read it; in Hermes it is added with skills.external_dirs. It is the same skills folder that --platform codex uses.
